import html # Predefined template for a forum post. # It contains placeholders for poster, heading, body and labels. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{heading}

Posted by: {poster}

{body}
{labels}
""" def create_forum_post(poster: str, heading: str, body: str, labels: list[str]) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- poster : str Author of the post. heading : str Title of the post. body : str Main content of the post. labels : list[str] List of tags to associate with the post. Returns ------- str A string containing safe HTML for rendering on a web page. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not of the expected type. """ # Basic type checking to catch programming errors early if not isinstance(poster, str): raise TypeError("poster must be a string") if not isinstance(heading, str): raise TypeError("heading must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise TypeError("body must be a string") if not isinstance(labels, list) or not all(isinstance(l, str) for l in labels): raise TypeError("labels must be a list of strings") # Escape user-supplied content to prevent XSS safe_poster = html.escape(poster, quote=True) safe_heading = html.escape(heading, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') # Build the tags section safe_labels = [] for label in labels: escaped_label = html.escape(label, quote=True) safe_labels.append(f'{escaped_label}') labels_html = ' '.join(safe_labels) # Format the final HTML return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster=safe_poster, heading=safe_heading, body=safe_body, labels=labels_html )
